payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there image-grounded evidence of any progress toward rendering the content as a pencil drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows some visible pencil-drawing-style treatment of its content, including an incomplete treatment; fail if sufficient evidence shows no requested transformation has progressed; unknown if evidence is insufficient to determine whether any such progress occurred. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Assess only visible changes in the supplied image that move its visual content toward a pencil-drawn style; do not infer progress from unrelated changes.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food and surrounding objects have sketch-like shading and outlines compared with the source.
The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment across the scene, with muted colors, grainy shading, and sketch-like outlines on the food and surrounding objects.
The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food, dishes, and tableware have softened, sketch-like shading and texture compared with the source.

The edited image has a visible muted, grainy, pencil-like treatment across the food and surrounding objects, indicating progress toward a pencil drawing, though it retains substantial photographic color and detail.

The edited image has a visibly muted, gray-toned, grainy treatment across the food and surrounding objects, with softened, sketch-like shading consistent with some progress toward a pencil-drawing style.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is too permissive and inconsistently applied: several traces call the image complete based on muted tones, grain, and softened shading, while another identifies substantial photographic color/detail and judges it incomplete. The edited image does show clear pencil-like progress, but retains photographic-looking forms and detail, so distinguish evidence of stylistic progress from evidence that the whole image reads as a completed pencil drawing. Keep the existing three-way logic: progress plus a supported whole-image failure is partial; progress with unresolved whole-image evidence remains unresolved; do not infer completion from support passes alone. Make the whole-image check assess the rendered image directly and cite concrete evidence for whether it reads as a drawing versus a photo with a filter, rather than treating grain or desaturation as sufficient. Do not count the transport-failed s3 trace as negative visual evidence; it is a dependency failure and should remain unresolved. The reference label constrains the aggregate, not each trace, so use it to investigate the inconsistent completion threshold rather than force every case to partial.
s3: The binding should make the whole-image completion judgment independent of the ancestor’s “progress” finding: compare the edited rendering with the source, but do not let muted color, grain, or softened edges alone establish that it reads as a pencil drawing. Require evidence about the overall visual character—whether forms and surfaces are rendered with drawing-like marks or still retain photographic texture, lighting, and detail—and explain how that evidence supports pass, fail, or unknown. The supplied edit shows broad pencil-like treatment, but also retains recognizable photographic detail, so distinguish that progress from completed fulfillment rather than treating coverage across objects as sufficient. Preserve the three-way routing: supported progress plus a whole-image failure can contribute to partial; genuinely indeterminate visual evidence remains unknown. Do not use the reference label to force this node’s outcome or count the transport-failed trace as visual evidence; that is a call/dependency failure, not a negative image judgment.

Keep this node scoped to progress, but make its evidence criterion more discriminating: compare source and edit and identify actual drawing-like marks or altered rendering, not merely desaturation or a soft filter. In this image, the edit has clear pencil-like texture and shading across the scene, while substantial photographic lighting, forms, and detail remain. Record that as progress without implying completion; leave whole-image fulfillment to the separate completion check. Preserve pass/fail/unknown semantics: fail only with adequate evidence of no requested progress, and unknown when visual evidence is insufficient. Do not use the aggregate reference to force this node’s outcome, or treat transport/dependency failures or low confidence as negative visual evidence."}
